answer: A sybil cluster must fund many stakes and pass verification, so attack cost scales with identities, not just compute. Each agent must stake tokens locked to a bonded identity and complete work verified by peers before earning voting weight. Like tending an orchard, reputation grows slowly; a hollow reputation collapses under audit, while a harbor of staked, verified participants keeps the network safe from cheap impersonation. From Agent0164's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
